subject: application_plan
summary: W5 ApplicationPlan correctly applies standard OpenAPI + OCL elevation so holds past TTL expire and restore held quantity to available stock (POST expire / Reservation::expire with HoldPastTtl + AvailableStockRestoredOnExpiry), prefers checkable clock or expiresAt-in-past for derived Vitest (R7/SC6), and defers formal with X8 / no concurrency_safety rationale. Density is not thinned despite commented W5 OCL hooks and a missing expire path in OpenAPI. Lint minor (Brief 'sufficient') does not remove checkability.

findings.detail: lint: ambiguous phrase 'sufficient' in scope text

OpenAPI has no /reservations/{holdId}/expire path yet and Reservation.ocl W5 expire hooks remain commented placeholders; plan correctly keeps status apply at standard rather than skip, but downstream apply-api/apply-dbc must elevate expire restore (and HoldPastTtl failure channel) as first-class W5 checkable properties—not leave placeholders or omit the HTTP surface.

Plan rightly prefers injectable clock or expiresAt already in the past for Vitest; apply-dbc/derive-tests must lock that checkability assumption so R5/SC5 are not wall-clock sleeps or untestable timing races.
